E4.justification: v2 adds reasoning ablations, safety/context-priority interventions, judge agreement and false-positive/false-negative analyses, and a code-output mismatch case study. The earlier long-context Gemini sweeps and 37-trace persona review are replaced by short-context scaling and analysis of a reported 264 traces, including keyword frequencies (Sections 4.4–4.6; Appendices A and C).

E5.justification: v1 explicitly reports single-run results without uncertainty intervals. v2 reports three runs for harmful-example experiments and ten runs/seeds for TruthfulQA experiments, with 95% normal confidence intervals; the separate Claude test remains single-run. Appendix A adds agreement statistics and Cohen's kappa. The retained 64-shot chart still lacks uncertainty intervals.

E6.justification: New results include 24.2% EM for Gemini 3 Pro with TruthfulQA examples and 1.2% with safety-priority prompting (Figures 3–4). Earlier long-context sweep results are removed, while the 64-shot scores survive unchanged as Figure 6. The 67.5% persona-rationalization statistic is replaced by a different 67% keyword statistic. Added Qwen3 Next 80B Thinking results are inconsistent: Figure 3 reports 0.034, whereas Table 11 reports 0.045.

M1.justification: The core demonstration-and-completion procedure is unchanged. Section 4.6 adds prompting variants that prepend 'Prioritize Safety' or 'Prioritize adhering to context', introducing a limited inference-time intervention and mitigation method.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion are substantially rewritten. Research questions are reformulated and explicitly mapped to six Results subsections instead of two. Experimental setup and appendices are reorganized around the expanded analyses, and the author list gains an additional equal-contribution author.

P2.justification: v2 revises Figure 1's examples and introduces full-width model and intervention charts, uncertainty bars/bands, and numerous reasoning, validation and example tables. The earlier long-context plots disappear. Retained material is matched across renumbering: v1 Figure 5 becomes v2 Figure 6, and v1 Table 3 becomes v2 Table 10.

R1.justification: v2 adds discussion of few-shot jailbreaking/defense and in-context data poisoning, plus RAG, tool-use, TruthfulQA and model references. It removes the Lanham et al. faithfulness and Jason Wei et al. chain-of-thought references. The central positioning against finetuning, steering and malicious-query jailbreaking remains substantially intact.

T1.justification: Neither version presents formal theorems, proofs or substantive mathematical derivations. The expanded safety/context-conflict hypothesis remains conceptual and experimentally tested; the added statistical reporting does not introduce new formal theory.

improvement.justification: Repeated runs, uncertainty reporting, zero-example controls and two-person judge validation substantially strengthen v1's single-run evidence and validation limited to flagged harmful outputs. Intervention experiments improve support for the mechanism hypothesis, and scaling claims become more cautious. Removing long-context sweeps loses useful evidence, while numerical inconsistencies remain, including Figure 3 versus Table 11. The generalized context-priority increase also needs qualification: Grok 4 falls from 7.7% to 7.3% in Figure 4. These shortcomings temper but do not outweigh the substantial gains in empirical support.

A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ICL-induced emergent-misalignment study. All nine v1 pages and sixteen v2 pages, including figures, tables, judge prompts and appendices, are readable and support reliable comparison.

after.justification: v2 reports original experiments with harmful and non-harmful examples, reasoning and prompting interventions, and human validation of 136 outputs (Section 4; Appendix A).

before.justification: v1 reports original four-model experiments, demonstration-count sweeps and analysis of 37 misaligned reasoning traces (Section 4 and appendices).

results.title: Emergent Misalignment via In-Context Learning: Narrow in-context examples can produce broadly misaligned LLMs

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: an MDP-based long-horizon SQL agent, execution/memory verification, self-taught SFT followed by RL, and superior CoSQL/SParC performance. Reworded contribution bullets and additional supporting experiments do not materially redefine these headline claims.

C2.justification: v3 substantially expands interpretation of deployment robustness, efficiency trade-offs, truncation failures, and real-time applicability. Section 5 and Appendix C.3 discuss industrial schema retrieval, alternative memory backends, and compatibility with large-model distillation pipelines as untested extensions. v2 already acknowledged higher token costs, but lacked these detailed applicability arguments and qualifications.

D1.justification: v3 newly identifies basic vLLM as the latency-measurement implementation and describes absent inference optimizations. A configuration comment clarifies that KL loss was already disabled. The release promise changes from after internal review to upon acceptance, with the explicit artifact list removed. Hardware, learning rates, tool templates, and most configuration details are retained.

E1.justification: v3 adds evaluation on Spider and BIRD using a CoSQL-trained model, plus a CoSQL scenario conditioned on model-generated prior SQL (Tables 6 and 12). These expand benchmark coverage and input conditions beyond v2. First-turn evaluation within CoSQL/SParC already existed; industrial scenarios discussed in v3 are not evaluated.

E2.justification: v3 Table 2 adds short-horizon Direct RL at 1.7B/4B and a LangGraph planning/tool agent, while dropping the Qwen3-8B rows and untrained long-horizon 14B row from that comparison. Table 12 introduces single-turn comparators including DAIL-SQL+GPT-4, CHASE-SQL+Gemini 1.5, and RESDSQL-3B+NatSQ. These substantially expand the evaluated comparison methods.

E3.justification: v3 introduces a LLaMA3.2-3B-Instruct setting, gold-versus-predicted-history testing, reward-component controls, and 2,000/4,000/6,000/8,000-token inference caps. Appendix D.6 specifies extracting intermediate SQL when truncation prevents completion. The efficiency comparison changes from v2 Table 8's averaged EX to CoSQL-specific evaluation in v3 Table 13; the original Qwen training configuration largely remains unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 adds reward-component ablations separating verification from proposal/correction rewards, token-budget sensitivity, and predicted-history robustness tests. Its error chart also adds the SFT-only stage between base and SFT+RL (Figure 6). The earlier tool ablations, turn/difficulty analyses, training dynamics, and case studies are retained, sometimes relocated.

E5.justification: v3 Table 10 introduces ± reporting for reward-ablation results, including 79.1±0.15 EX for the previously reported outcome-only result of 79.1. Neither the meaning of these quantities nor run counts or seeds is specified, so additional runs and statistical significance cannot be inferred.

E6.justification: Substantial new results include predicted-history CoSQL EX of 76.5 versus Direct RL's 71.2, Spider/BIRD EX of 84.2/56.9, and architectural-transfer, reward-ablation, and token-budget outcomes. Most original Table 2 cells remain, but the full 4B model's out-of-domain CoSQL EM changes from 62.9 to 63.0, alongside edited averages. The replacement efficiency results use different settings and do not establish same-setting improvements.

M1.justification: Section 3.3.2 changes the stated reward aggregation from four separately weighted terms to two groups: EX plus EM, and all process rewards. The action loop, self-taught SFT algorithm, and GRPO procedure remain intact. This establishes a limited objective revision, without establishing that retained experiments were rerun.

P1.justification: RQ1 is substantially reordered into grouped effectiveness, generalization/robustness, and efficiency arguments. Training dynamics moves from Section 4.5 to Appendix D.8, Algorithm 1 moves to Appendix A, and a Discussion section is introduced. The appendix organization is extensively revised, alongside terminology standardization and prose tightening.

P2.justification: Table 2 is reorganized by backbone and reasoning horizon, removes its combined Average column, and adds comparison rows. v3 introduces several evaluation tables and two Pareto plots, and redraws the error chart with an SFT-only series. Original figures are extensively redistributed between main text and appendices, with difficulty accuracy also displayed separately.

R1.justification: v3 adds references supporting DAIL-SQL, RESDSQL, CHASE-SQL, LLaMA, and production-agent latency discussion. Section 4.4 also changes attribution of the error taxonomy from prior work to the authors' design. The main related-work positioning remains stable; merged duplicate SQL-R1 references and publication updates do not represent different cited works.

T1.justification: The total-reward definition in Section 3.3.2 now imposes shared coefficients within outcome and process groups, replacing four coefficients with two. This changes the formal weighting specification. The MDP definitions, transition structure, and SFT/GRPO expressions otherwise remain substantively unchanged; Algorithm 1 is relocated rather than newly introduced.

improvement.justification: v3 addresses important gaps in v2's empirical support through trained Direct RL controls, component-level reward ablations, and testing with model-generated dialogue histories. Transfer and token-budget experiments further strengthen assessment of generality and practical costs. These substantially improve the evidence for the framework despite narrower latency-comparator coverage, unexplained ± quantities, and limited implementation detail for some new baselines.

A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MTSQL-R1. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including material relocated between versions.

after.justification: v3 retains original experiments and adds baseline comparisons, transfer evaluations, predicted-history testing, reward ablations, and inference-budget experiments.

before.justification: v2 reports original CoSQL/SParC experiments, training-stage and tool ablations, error analyses, training dynamics, and case studies.

results.title: MTSQL-R1: Towards Long-Horizon Multi-Turn Text-to-SQL via Agentic Training

C1.justification: The central claims remain localized reasoning uncertainty, training-free selective CFG, efficient negative-prompt guidance through KV-cache reuse, and improved reasoning with minimal overhead. The abstract and contribution list replace Qwen performance examples with DeepSeek and Ling examples, but preserve the meaning and scope of these core contributions.

C2.justification: V2 develops a distribution-ranking explanation distinguishing MTI from standard sampling, attributes reduced latency to shorter reasoning trajectories, and interprets the new entropy-scope, CD, and domain-specific prompt experiments. Section 6 newly acknowledges threshold tuning and recommends a preliminary data sweep. These additions substantially expand mechanism explanations and practical qualifications beyond v1.

D1.justification: V2 identifies the two reported LiveCodeBench subtasks, specifies official VLM prompts and threshold 2.0, and describes single-GPU timing. It removes the WinoGrande and HellaSwag configuration links and describes the unchanged negative cue as adding two auxiliary tokens rather than three. These are limited documentation changes; the supplied code link remains the same.

E1.justification: Section 4.5 adds multimodal spatial-understanding coverage through Where2Place, RefSpatial, and VaBenchPoint, substantially extending the original text-based tasks. WinoGrande disappears from the main accuracy table but remains explicitly included in the new latency experiment. The principal knowledge, mathematics, and coding benchmarks are retained.

E2.justification: V1 compares MTI against Direct Inference and Vanilla CFG. V2 retains these and adds reported comparisons with TALE, NoThinking, Dynasor, DEER, and CGRS on three benchmarks in Table 5. Table 7 additionally evaluates vanilla contrastive decoding against MTI(CD), substantially broadening the comparator set.

E3.justification: The main evaluation matrix removes Qwen3-Base blocks and adds DeepSeek-R1-7B and Ling-mini-2.0 configurations; spatial experiments introduce Qwen3-8B-VL-Instruct. The guidance-strength and prompt ablations change from Qwen3-8B on GPQA-Diamond to DeepSeek across three datasets, and a latency evaluation is introduced. The 32768 context limit and principal greedy and stochastic decoding settings are retained.

E4.justification: V2 adds explicit low-versus-high entropy intervention controls, CFG-versus-CD substitution experiments, task-specific and meaningless-prompt tests, and latency analysis. Figure 3 replaces the original Qwen ablations with revised DeepSeek analyses. The original entropy-modification analysis and mathematical case study are retained, with the case study moved to Appendix A.5; the base-model word-cloud panels are removed.

E5.justification: Both versions report means over eight independent stochastic AIME2024 runs. V2 extends this reporting practice to additional models without documenting an increased run count. Neither version provides confidence intervals, variability estimates, or significance tests.

E6.justification: V2 adds extensive model, spatial, latency, comparator, and diagnostic results while removing Qwen3-Base result blocks. New Table 1 reports DeepSeek DI at 61.70 and MTI at 70.98 with threshold 0.5; Table 2 reports Ling AIME2024 increasing from 60.00 to 71.25. Matched Qwen AIME2024 scores are retained. Main-table averages change alongside coverage and cannot establish same-setting gains. Section 4.2's DeepSeek value of 70.73 conflicts with Table 1.

M1.justification: The primary entropy-gated CFG procedure, negative-prompt injection, and KV-cache reuse remain unchanged. Appendix A.3 adds an evaluated MTI(CD) variant that replaces CFG with contrastive decoding, constituting a limited procedural extension.

P1.justification: The related-work discussion, methodological preliminaries, main-results narrative, and ablation explanations undergo extensive rewriting. Contributions are consolidated, the case study moves to the appendix, a limitations section is introduced, and the appendix develops from a configuration list into eight subsections. This materially changes the narrative and organization.

P2.justification: The main tables are restructured and gain green highlighting, Figure 3 is redrawn for revised experiments, and six additional tables present new evaluations and analyses. The word-cloud display contracts from four panels to two, the entropy and word-cloud figures are renumbered, and the existing case-study figure moves to the appendix.

R1.justification: Section 2 and new Appendix A.7 substantially expand positioning against confidence-based scaling, contrastive decoding, speculative decoding, and sampling strategies. New references include DeepConf, EGB, the five additional test-time comparators, and spatial VLM research. The revision explains MTI's relationship to these approaches beyond the original related-work discussion.

T1.justification: Equation 2 corrects the missing minus sign in Shannon entropy, repairing a mathematical error in v1. V2 also explicitly documents the existing answer-entropy aggregation and the CD formulation. No new theorem, proof, or substantial theoretical development is introduced.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens validation of the central accuracy and efficiency claims. Table 3 supplies measured latency where v1 relied on CFG usage as a cost proxy, while additional model families, comparison methods, and entropy-scope controls address important gaps in generality and mechanism evidence. These gains outweigh the loss of Qwen3-Base coverage and remaining reporting weaknesses, including the 70.73 versus 70.98 inconsistency. Uncertainty estimates and precise timing hardware remain unspecified.

A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MTI research, with matching title, authors, and core framework. Their complete texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

after.justification: V2 retains original experimental results and adds DeepSeek and Ling evaluations, spatial vision-language experiments, latency measurements, and further comparisons and ablations.

before.justification: V1 reports original Qwen3 benchmark evaluations, hyperparameter ablations, token-entropy analyses, and a qualitative reasoning case study.

results.title: Less is More: Improving LLM Reasoning with Minimal Test-Time Intervention

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction extend the performance claim beyond GRPO variants to external-guidance methods, notably LTE† outperforming LUFFY under aligned settings. v2 qualifies independence as absence of explicit reasoning-trace guidance. The conclusion drops its contrast-optimization claim and categorical reward-hacking-free wording.

C2.justification: v2 replaces the missing-entropy-control limitation with the 8,192-token training limit. It removes the small-data/overfitting explanation for weaker 8B results, tentatively attributes poor EvoCoT/ReLIFT results to model compatibility, and explains Qwen2.5/Llama exclusions. The central interpretation of LTE promoting exploration remains.

D1.justification: v2 adds code-access information, host hardware and operating-system details, eight H20 GPUs, training times of roughly 6–9 days, and artifact licenses. Appendix B updates training hyperparameters and specifies LUFFY's entropy coefficient. These substantially expand reproducibility documentation; the hardware information is newly disclosed, not an established hardware change.

E1.justification: Training coverage changes from separate difficulty-selected Skywork-OR1-RL-Data subsets for the two models to a common OpenR1-Math-46k-8192 corpus. This replaces the central training data, while mathematical reasoning and all six evaluation benchmarks remain unchanged.

E2.justification: v2 Tables 1–2 add evaluated EvoCoT, ReLIFT, DAPO and LUFFY comparisons for both model sizes. The entropy-enabled GRPO and GRPO-plus-extra-rollout comparisons disappear. GRPOExtra is the renamed existing extra-rollout baseline, not a new comparator.

E3.justification: Training changes from 300 to 500 steps and from a 16,384-token to an 8,192-token response limit; final-checkpoint evaluation changes accordingly. Model-specific difficulty subsets are replaced by the common 45,792-instance corpus. v2 also introduces separate hint-removal controls for the 8B ablation. Benchmark sampling and decoding settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Section 5.4 and Table 3 isolate incorrect-answer hints and overlong-response hints, providing component-specific evidence absent from v1. Training-sample and dynamics analyses are revised for the new experiments, while v1's all-pass sample analysis and Figure 3c are removed.

E5.justification: Both versions retain four or sixteen sampled responses per evaluation problem and report point estimates. Neither supplies independent training-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. The confidence-level discussion in Appendix A is theoretical, not empirical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Most trained-model results are replaced: for example, entropy-free 8B LTE averages are 41.11/53.87 for Pass@1/Pass@k in v1 versus 49.01/66.78 in v2. These use different training conditions and are not same-setting gains. New baseline and ablation results appear, and GRPO's average Pass@k changes from below to above the base models.

M1.justification: The hinted extra rollouts, truncation-dependent prompts, replacement with successful responses and mixed-policy objective remain unchanged. Algorithm 1 is identical apart from terminology. LTE† renames the existing entropy-enabled variant; the new ablations test existing components.

P1.justification: The overall section order and methodological exposition remain largely intact. v2 standardizes terminology and variant names, edits the introduction and results narrative, adds a learning analogy, and condenses related-work and conclusion prose. A dedicated ablation subsection and expanded ethical-considerations paragraphs provide bounded structural additions.

P2.justification: v2 adds an introductory illustration and ablation/license tables, restructures the main result tables with an entropy-control column, and removes the training-statistics table. Training plots receive revised axes and legends; the all-pass panel disappears and the entropy plot focuses on the late-training range. Existing framework and prompt diagrams are retained and renumbered.

R1.justification: Related work adds reasoning hints from Chen et al., theorem-proving feedback from Thakur et al., and offline mistakes from Alazraki et al. Model-selection discussion adds Qwen2.5, Llama and contamination references; Yue et al. is removed. The four related-work categories and basic self-generated-guidance positioning remain.

T1.justification: v2 removes Appendix A.3's entire information-gain argument and Equations 22–25. Appendix A.2 removes the left-hand exponent n from Equation 19 and changes the stated assumption from alpha ~ Omega(1) to alpha > Omega(1/n). These alter both the scope and premises of the theoretical support.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens empirical support through direct hint-component ablations and comparisons with advanced and external-guidance methods, addressing important gaps in v1's validation. New code-access and computational details improve reproduction guidance, and the abstract's GRPO margins now match the tables. Losing entropy-enabled GRPO comparisons and unresolved EvoCoT/ReLIFT compatibility concerns limit the evidence, but the added component and comparative tests provide a substantial net gain. Higher cross-version scores alone do not establish improvement because training conditions changed.

A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LTE research work. All 12 pages of each version, including figures, tables, equations and Appendices A–B, are readable and support reliable comparison.

after.justification: v2 reports original benchmark comparisons, training-dynamics analyses and component ablations in Tables 1–3 and Figures 4–5.

before.justification: v1 reports original Qwen3-4B/8B training experiments, results on six mathematical benchmarks, and training-dynamics analyses in Tables 1 and 3 and Figures 3–4.

results.title: Do Not Step Into the Same River Twice: Learning to Reason from Trial and Error

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the same central contributions: sequential claim-level factuality assessment, differentiated claim categories, improvements across four benchmarks and eight models, and the human-annotated dataset. The rewritten conclusion foregrounds ablation interpretations already present in v1 rather than establishing a different core claim.

C2.justification: v3 substantially qualifies contradiction detection, explaining how decomposition can obscure discourse cues and explicitly acknowledging that verification lacks full dialogue history. It adds an overthinking hypothesis for reasoning models and interpretations of partial abstentions, extraction failures, and CoCoNot annotation problems. These are substantive applicability and mechanism discussions beyond v1's limitations.

D1.justification: v3 replaces the repository placeholder with a concrete code/data reference and adds extensive implementation and annotation documentation: Python and libraries, 4-bit inference, decoding and reasoning settings, computational cost, baseline implementation, recruitment, and interface screenshots. These primarily disclose existing procedures. However, v1's explicit statement that each main benchmark uses 500 randomly sampled test conversations is omitted.

E1.justification: v3 adds CoCoNot refusal detection without retrieved documents or dialogue history and RGM-Contradictions evaluation of conversational inconsistency without retrieval. These substantially broaden the tested scenarios beyond the retained four grounded-dialogue benchmarks. Appendix G also identifies non-English items within the CoCoNot evaluation.

E2.justification: FActScore and LLM-as-Judge remain the comparators on the four original benchmarks. The new RGM comparison includes a 50% random baseline alongside LLM-as-Judge (v3 Table 5). The expanded FActScore-lite description documents the previously described turn-level adaptation rather than establishing a new comparator.

E3.justification: Section 7 introduces two balanced evaluations with 250 examples per class. CoCoNot excludes Incomplete and Indeterminate categories, supplies empty reference/history inputs, and evaluates abstention specifically. RGM adds contradiction-focused accuracy, precision, recall, and F1 reporting, including DeepSeek V3.2 and low-reasoning GPT-5 configurations.

E4.justification: v3 adds per-model category confusion matrices, detailed CoCoNot false-positive and false-negative analyses with examples, and an investigation of reasoning models on contradiction detection. The original FaithDial component ablations remain unchanged; the earlier annotation-discrepancy analysis and Chainsmokers example are retained in relocated appendices.

E5.justification: Appendix B.4 newly states that each experiment uses one evaluation pass without averaging across seeds and explains decoding determinism. This is additional run-count disclosure, not evidence that run counts changed. Existing McNemar tests and inter-annotator agreement statistics are retained.

E6.justification: The original benchmark, human-classification, and ablation scores are retained. New results include 90.6% CoCoNot accuracy and substantial contradiction weaknesses: GPT-5 (LR) scores 54.20% accuracy with VISTA versus 89.40% with LLM-as-Judge (v3 Table 5). Appendices F–G add detailed result counts. The erroneous Llama-70B/BEGIN significance marker against LLM-as-Judge is removed, while its underlying paired-test result remains unchanged.

M1.justification: v3 adds an optional fourth prompting stage that uses GPT-5 or DeepSeek V3.2 to check turn-level contradictions against full conversation history (Section 7.2; Appendix A.1.4). This is a targeted procedural extension; the original decomposition, verification, categorization, and memory pipeline remains.

P1.justification: v3 condenses and rewrites methodology and dataset descriptions, substantially recasts the conclusion, and replaces the main Discussion section with targeted evaluations while relocating retained discussion to Appendix H. Annotation material and supplementary sections are extensively reorganized. The title also shortens VISTA Score to VISTA.

P2.justification: v3 adds the contradiction-results table, eight category confusion matrices, two abstention-analysis tables, and annotation-interface screenshots. Existing annotation tables move to Appendix D. Figure 2 is reformatted with larger labels and a revised legend, and prompt appendices change from single-column to two-column layout; Figure 1 remains unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds citations for CoCoNot, RGM-Contradictions, HaluEval, and reasoning-model overthinking, including an explanation for excluding HaluEval. It removes the Dinan et al. Wizard-of-Wikipedia reference. The broader positioning relative to decomposition methods and LLM judges remains largely unchanged.

T1.justification: No substantive mathematical definitions, assumptions, theorems, proofs, or derivations are added or revised. The quadratic equation appearing in v3 Appendix G belongs to a quoted dataset response, not the paper's theoretical analysis.

improvement.justification: v1's human evaluation contained only 22 abstention and eight contradiction claims. v3's dedicated 500-item evaluations substantially strengthen scrutiny of these defining capabilities, exposing serious contradiction weaknesses alongside strong abstention accuracy. Detailed error analyses and implementation documentation improve interpretability and reproducibility. The auxiliary settings imperfectly match the intended RAG setting, and some English/RAG-only scope statements remain inconsistent, but the gains in empirical scrutiny and transparency are substantial.

A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VISTA research work. Their complete main texts and appendices, including figures, tables, and prompt templates, support reliable comparison despite substantial reorganization.

after.justification: v3 retains those original results and adds CoCoNot abstention and RGM-Contradictions evaluations, confusion matrices, and error analyses.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations across eight models and four benchmarks, human annotations of 888 claims, and FaithDial ablation results.

results.title: VISTA: Verification In Sequential Turn-based Assessment

C1.justification: The central contribution remains fully synthetic adaptation through categorized exploration and dual refinement. v2 broadens the empirical claim beyond controlled websites, explicitly claiming generalization to live websites without target-specific synthesis or retraining. The abstract's principal superiority claim and the conclusion otherwise retain their scope and meaning.

C2.justification: v2 substantially expands interpretation to live-site generalization, consistency across judges, and the benefits of constrained reordering. Its ablation discussion shifts from task refinement's marginal 0.88-point cumulative gain to its largest individual removal loss of 4.87 points, under different contrasts. Explorer's failure explanation is also qualified by newly disclosed authentication support. Some claims of stable cross-judge rankings exceed what the tables establish.

D1.justification: New Appendix A.4 documents baseline code adaptation and Explorer authentication handling, while A.3 elaborates reordering checks. The abstract changes the code-release statement from future availability to stated public availability. Conversely, the explicit statement about restarting the environment for every evaluation run disappears. These disclosures do not establish changes to the retained experiments.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates only the five controlled WebArena websites. v2 adds Online-Mind2Web, comprising 300 tasks across 136 live websites, evaluated without target-site synthesis or retraining. This substantially expands evaluation from adaptation within controlled environments to transfer into live website environments.

E2.justification: The main comparison retains the same baselines and Table 1 results. Within the corresponding ablation comparison, however, v2 Table 5 drops the explicit naive synthetic-supervision (+SS) comparator shown in v1 Table 4. Its matching OS-Genesis results remain in Table 1; this is a limited change in comparison membership.

E3.justification: v2 introduces live-site evaluation using GPT-4.1, GPT-5.1, and WebJudge, and expands synthetic-data assessment from GPT-4.1 alone to three judges, including Qwen3-30B. It also introduces a paired evaluation of 100 reordered trajectories and component-removal controls. The retained WebArena split, training budgets, and model configurations remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The cumulative ablation in v1 Table 4 becomes a component-removal study in v2 Table 5, adding isolated removal of categorized exploration and task refinement. Existing configurations are retained under matching names. New analyses examine category granularity, editing-operation frequencies, reordering quality, and robustness across judges; Appendix B adds representative category sets.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests for the experiments. v2 adds descriptive statistics and averages across judges, but these do not provide estimates of experimental uncertainty.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial results, including 23.56 average Online-Mind2Web success for SynthAgent, new ablation outcomes, additional judge scores, and reordering quality scores of 68.9 versus 62.1. Table 1 is unchanged, and v1's GPT-4.1 quality scores are retained in v2 Table 10. Section 5.1 corrects completion-rate prose from 92.5% to 96.5%, matching the unchanged completion table.

M1.justification: The four-stage procedure, conflict-triggered task refinement, conservative trajectory editing, and supervised fine-tuning objective remain unchanged. Independence conditions for reordering already appear in v1. The stronger emphasis and additional implementation explanations in v2 do not establish a procedural change; all six appendix prompts are unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 extensively rewrites the introduction around a grounding-versus-trajectory-noise tension, revises related-work and method explanations, compresses the trajectory-edit list into prose, and rewrites the ablation discussion. Appendix A inserts new analysis and implementation subsections before the retained generation descriptions. The conclusion and appendix prompts remain unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 substantially reorganizes quantitative presentation through new benchmark and analysis tables, a main quality table combining judge-specific scores with averages, relocation of the original quality table, and a redesigned ablation table. Table 1 and Figure 3 are reduced in size; all six figures retain their content. New appendix result tables duplicate the retained prompt-table labels 7–11, making references ambiguous.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to Synatra, NNetNav, AgentOccam, Online-Mind2Web's associated work, and the Qwen3 technical report. Section 2.3 adds short substantive comparisons with Synatra and NNetNav. OS-Genesis and Explorer remain the principal research comparators, so the broader positioning changes only modestly.

T1.justification: The problem formulation, conflict predicate in Equation 1, and supervised fine-tuning loss in Equation 2 are unchanged. Neither version contains additional theorems or proofs. The revised discussion of refinement synergy and independent edits adds explanation rather than new mathematical reasoning.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens empirical support beyond v1's controlled-WebArena evaluation and single-judge quality assessment. Live-site transfer, additional judges, component-removal ablations, and the reordering comparison address important gaps in applicability and component validation. Baseline implementation disclosures also improve assessability. Overstated cross-judge consistency claims and new duplicate table labels weaken precision and navigation, but the stronger empirical evidence provides a clear substantial net improvement.

A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SynthAgent research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching despite revisions and duplicated table labels in v2.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds Online-Mind2Web evaluation, additional ablations, exploration statistics, trajectory-reordering comparisons, and assessments by additional judges.

before.justification: v1 reports original WebArena experiments, synthetic-data quality and trajectory-completion measurements, component ablations, and data-scaling results.

results.title: SynthAgent: Adapting Web Agents with Synthetic Supervision

C1.justification: The central contributions remain Cognitive Alpha Mining through code-based LLM evolution, a seven-level agent hierarchy and quality checking, with claims of predictive strength, stability and interpretability. The expanded dataset evidence supports these retained claims without introducing a different principal contribution.

C2.justification: Section 4.2 replaces the Alpha360 stability explanation with an argument that more factors need not improve prediction, and explains Random Forest's RankICIR advantage through stability. New passages discuss market-dependent thresholds and hyperparameter diversity. The Limitations section adds specific qualifications concerning simulated trading, stochastic reproducibility and computational scaling.

D1.justification: v2 substantially expands reproducibility information: 20-factor combinations, rolling step 126, LightGBM/Ridge hyperparameters, runtime and single-H100 details, specific leakage checks, additional data sources, and MarketCycle plus crossover/mutation prompts. These mostly document previously described procedures. The abstract's promise to release all source code disappears, although the future prompt-repository statement remains; neither PDF provides a CogAlpha repository link.

E1.justification: Coverage expands from CSI300 large-cap Chinese equities to CSI500 smaller Chinese companies, U.S. S&P500 stocks and Hong Kong HSI/HSCI stocks. Appendix B.1 and Table 5 establish actual evaluations across these additional populations and markets.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains all 19 original baselines and adds evaluated AutoAlpha (Kou et al., 2024) and AlphaAgent comparisons. These introduce directly relevant automated alpha-mining frameworks absent from v1's reported comparisons. Both works were already cited in v1, which called the Kou method AutoGPT.

E3.justification: New evaluations introduce a 30-day CSI300 target, Ridge factor combination, additional market-specific chronological splits and controlled variations of population and generation settings. Appendix A.4 specifies a lower S&P500 MI floor, 0.012 versus CSI300's 0.02. Existing CSI300 dates, metrics and backtest costs remain unchanged; newly disclosed rolling-training and factor-count details do not establish changes to the original experiments.

E4.justification: The original component ablation, threshold sensitivity and liquidity-evolution example are retained. v2 adds an eight-configuration AgentMarketCycle sensitivity study covering parent-pool size, generation count and sub-cycle length (Table 4), three elite-factor cases with training/test measurements (Listings 4–6), and a computational-cost comparison in Appendix B.5.

E5.justification: Appendix B.6 newly states that reported outcomes follow a single round of factor mining and discusses LLM randomness. v1 supplies no corresponding run-count statement. Neither version reports repeated-run confidence intervals or significance tests; this is additional disclosure, not evidence of changed replication.

E6.justification: Original Table 1 and component-ablation scores remain, while v2 adds comparator, sensitivity, cross-market, runtime and elite-factor results. New 30-day CSI300 LightGBM results are IC 0.0886 and RankIC 0.1243; the original 10-day values remain 0.0591 and 0.0814, so these are different settings. v2 also acknowledges Random Forest's higher RankICIR, 0.4385 versus 0.4350, and revises the strong single-factor finding to refer to absolute correlations.

M1.justification: Section 3.5 changes adaptive guidance from the top two valid alphas to two randomly selected valid alphas. Appendix B.4 additionally introduces plateau-based early stopping alongside fixed-generation evolution. The core hierarchy, quality checker, fitness selection and evolutionary operators remain; expanded checker descriptions and prompts mainly disclose existing components.

P1.justification: Most original prose and the main section sequence are retained. Local rewrites clarify the meaning of cognitive reasoning, revise the baseline discussion and correct author/prompt terminology. Supporting material is reorganized into expanded appendices, and Limitations and Ethical Considerations sections are added.

P2.justification: The document switches from a single-column layout to two columns, extensively reflowing text, equations, code and prompt boxes. Table 1 gains dataset/horizon columns and comparator rows; Tables 4–5 and Listings 4–6 are added. The hierarchy diagram, ablation table, threshold plot and existing evolution listings move into appendices while retaining their underlying content.

R1.justification: v2 adds Verbalized Sampling (Zhang et al., 2025) to motivate generation diversity, together with Hong Kong index and yfinance references. The principal related-work coverage and positioning against formula-based alpha mining and evolutionary LLM research remain substantially unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix B.4 newly defines the plateau statistic delta = mean(curr) - mean(prev), with termination when delta <= 0.001. This is a limited mathematical specification of the stopping rule. Existing factor and evaluation-metric equations are otherwise retained, and no theorem or proof is added.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially addresses v1's narrow CSI300 validation and lack of evaluated competing alpha-mining frameworks through Tables 1 and 5. The new sensitivity study and detailed implementation/prompt appendices strengthen empirical scrutiny and reproducibility, while the corrected Random Forest comparison improves accuracy. Uncertainty remains unquantified and the blanket code-release promise is removed, but these limitations do not outweigh the substantial validation and documentation gains.

A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CogAlpha research. Their complete main texts and Appendices A–C are readable, and the equations, tables, figures and relocated analyses can be matched reliably.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds evaluations across additional stock markets, training methods and prediction horizons, plus hyperparameter and generated-factor analyses.

before.justification: v1 reports original CSI300 prediction and backtesting results, component ablations, threshold sensitivity and alpha-evolution measurements.

results.title: Cognitive Alpha Mining via LLM-Driven Code-Based Evolution

C1.justification: The central framing shifts from disentangling truth into style/substance to verdict-anchored control of deceptive explanations and faithfulness hallucinations. v3 adds performance-adaptive cross-model transfer and divergence amplification as main contributions, while dropping v1's headline distinction between middle-layer human-unknown truths and higher-layer human-observable truths.

C2.justification: v3 adds interpretations linking transfer success to source-model performance and steering gains to KV/IV divergence. It reframes faithfulness as contextual/logical consistency and revises the explanation of middle-layer effects. New substantive limitations address model scale, coarse labels, outdated internal knowledge, and unavailable suitable time-shifted explanation data.

D1.justification: v3 adds a code-access link, explicit steering search ranges and failure thresholds, per-setting optimal layers and multipliers, and the automatic judge's exact model version (Appendices C/F/O; Tables 18–19). These substantially fill steering-specific reproducibility gaps. Most training hyperparameters and hardware information were already present in v1.

E1.justification: Both versions use RAW-FC, LIAR-RAW, and AVeriTeC for the same claim-verification and explanation tasks. The new transfer and Mistral experiments reuse these datasets; the 'in-the-wild' result concerns transferring vectors between dataset-specific models, without introducing another data population or task.

E2.justification: v3 adds DeReC to the RAW-FC comparison, reporting 64.61 Macro-F in Table 9. Existing RAW-FC comparators remain, but LLaMA2-7B-Chat, non-Google FactLLaMA, and L-Defense with LLaMA2 lose their LIAR-RAW verdict entries because the appendix comparison covers only RAW-FC. The principal comparator set otherwise remains stable.

E3.justification: v3 introduces transfer protocols between RAW-FC- and LIAR-RAW-trained models, Mistral-v0.1 configurations, and blinded, position-swapped pairwise judgments by three annotators across all three test sets. These substantially expand evaluation design beyond v1's protocols. Original splits and training settings largely remain; Qwen's reported size changes from 7B to 8B without establishing reruns.

E4.justification: v3 adds probability-gap versus performance validation, KV/IV direction-similarity analysis, explanation-quality breakdowns by vector and correctness, transfer failure analysis, and multiple faithfulness case studies (Section 5; Appendices D, M–T). The original layer, direction, recency-bias, and explanation-length analyses are retained, often relocated.

E5.justification: v3 adds bootstrap means and 95% confidence intervals for RAW-FC ablations, standard errors for explanation-score changes, and annotator-agreement estimates: Cronbach's alpha 0.7896 and Fleiss' kappa 0.6963. These substantially expand uncertainty and reliability reporting beyond v1. Additional independent training runs or seeds are not established.

E6.justification: New transfer results include gains of 7.54 and losses of 17.95 Macro-F points relative to target SFT models (Table 17); new Mistral results reach 50.91 versus 42.03 for SFT (Table 20). The headline LIAR-RAW score changes from 43.61 to 50.59 through a different transfer configuration, not a same-setting improvement. Human scores, correlation coefficients, and some appendix Qwen statistics also change.

M1.justification: The training, quadrant selection, probing, and explanation-refinement pipeline is retained. However, v1 specifies positive KV steering, while v3 specifies negative-KV suppression/subtraction but retains backbone-correct Q4 activations as positive and reports signed multipliers. These inconsistent conventions leave unclear whether the intervention changed or its description changed (Section 3.4; v3 Appendices C/O).

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, background, and conclusion are extensively rewritten around faithfulness. Methodological details and existing analyses are reorganized into expanded appendices, and separate analysis, limitations, ethics, acknowledgments, and author-contribution material changes the narrative structure substantially.

P2.justification: v3 changes the publication layout, redraws the framework diagram, adds motivating and baseline schematics, human-comparison charts, vector-similarity plots, and tables with computational-cost columns. Existing displays are also relocated: v1's layer and token visualizations reappear as v3 Figures 9 and 7.

R1.justification: v3 substantially expands positioning around explanation faithfulness and hallucination, adding works such as Jacovi and Goldberg, Atanasova et al., and Kim et al. It develops contrasts with ITI/CAA and discusses DeReC and JustiLM, while removing or reducing v1's traditional explainability, self-training/STaR, and DoLa/TruthfulQA positioning.

T1.justification: v3 Appendix G and Table 9 add operation-count and asymptotic-complexity arguments, contrasting REFLEX's O(m) inference with O(mn) or O(mZ) alternatives. Most existing mathematical definitions remain, and no substantial theorem or proof development is introduced. The rewritten steering formalization also introduces the KV sign ambiguity noted under M1.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially addresses v1's limited validation through full-test human comparisons with agreement estimates, bootstrap uncertainty, and direct transfer tests exposing both gains and severe failures. Steering documentation and explicit applicability limitations improve auditability. The KV sign ambiguity and correlational mechanism arguments remain weaknesses, but the expanded validation materially strengthens the evidence available to assess effectiveness and its limits.

A1.justification: Both PDFs describe REFLEX and share its core framework, datasets, and original experiments. The complete main texts, figures, tables, equations, and appendices support comparison despite substantial rewriting and expansion.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and adds transfer experiments, Mistral results, broader human evaluation, bootstrap estimates, and steering-vector analyses.

before.justification: v1 reports original fact-checking and explanation-quality results, backbone and steering ablations, human evaluation, and case analysis in Section 4 and the appendices.

results.title: REFLEX: Self-Refining Explainable Fact-Checking via Verdict-Anchored Style Control

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution bullets and conclusion retain the same central contributions: robust representation interventions, query-adaptive routing and shared-subspace control for scalable lifelong knowledge editing. The additional evaluations support these claims without redefining the main contribution.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations distinguishing semantic routing from lexical matching, explaining interference at larger perturbation radii, and attributing narrower ZsRE advantages to shorter generation requirements. It also argues for protection through query rejection and limited effects of false activation. New Section 9 explicitly acknowledges untested extreme-scale knowledge bases and unassessed adversarial-editing and bias risks.

D1.justification: Table 8 newly specifies learning rate 0.01, 1,000 epochs, radius 0.02 and maximum cluster size 16, while consolidating the previously indicated rank and intervention layer. v2 also specifies fp32 for storage reporting and supplies training-time measurements. These fill important reproducibility gaps without establishing that existing training settings changed. The EasyEdit and Gemini access pointers remain unchanged.

E1.justification: v2 extends evaluation from unstructured editing on UnKE and EditEverything to structured editing on ZsRE. It also tests lexically similar, semantically different hard negatives within UnKE. These extend task and test-scenario coverage; the original datasets and MMLU evaluation remain.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds GRACE for both models, adds WISE to the Qwen comparison, and removes LoRA from the Llama comparison despite retaining its appendix description. Table 2 narrows the resource comparison by removing AnyEdit, UnKE and MEMIT, retaining WISE. The EditEverything comparator set is unchanged.

E3.justification: v2 adds a 3,000-edit ZsRE protocol with reliability, generalization, locality and average scores; lexical-similarity-based hard-negative selection; and router checks using 1,000 paraphrases and 5,000 MMLU queries. Resource evaluation changes from parameter counts to storage costs and adds training-time/peak-memory measurements. The retained UnKE batch size, temperature and gating threshold are unchanged, while the reported checkpoints omit T=1.

E4.justification: v2 adds tests of semantic locality against hard negatives (A.1), radius-induced interference (A.6.2), and relevant versus irrelevant router activation (A.7.1). It removes v1 A.1's forgetting analysis over 100 edits in batches of 10. The loss ablation, layer study, cluster-threshold analysis, routing-scalability study and generated-answer cases are retained or relocated.

E5.justification: Both versions use point estimates and empirical distributions, including the same spread annotations in Figure 1. Neither reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. The new hard-negative means and medians summarize added analysis results without introducing uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Retained UnKE, EditEverything and Tables 3–4 scores are unchanged. v2 adds baseline rows and ZsRE results, including RILKE averages of 0.88 on Llama and 0.85 on Qwen, while removing LoRA and T=1 results. It replaces parameter-count results with storage costs and adds radius, routing and training-cost outcomes, including 58 seconds per edit and 19 GB peak memory. These are newly reported results, not demonstrated same-setting performance gains.

M1.justification: Sections 4.2–4.3 change the specified individual and cluster routing rules from minimizing squared Euclidean distance to maximizing cosine similarity. The intervention map, KL-regularized objective and clustering procedure remain unchanged. The relevance gate newly explained in the method section was already present in v1 Section 5.2.

P1.justification: Substantial paragraph rewriting spans the abstract, introduction, motivation, method, experiments and related work. Section 3 is reorganized around semantic locality and the geometric properties. v2 adds a limitations section and reorganizes appendix material into cost, configuration and routing subsections, moving the layer study out of the main text.

P2.justification: Table 1 is redesigned for ZsRE and revised comparators, and Table 2 becomes a storage comparison. v2 adds cost, configuration and radius tables plus a hard-negative figure, redraws the framework and PCA illustrations, relocates the layer figure and removes the forgetting figure. Much of the appendix changes from full-width prose to two-column layout.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations concerning activation steering, ZsRE and editing risks, including Rimsky et al., Levy et al., BadEdit and ripple-effect evaluation, while removing the SheetDesigner and predictive-analysis citations. Its central positioning relative to weight-space and representation-based editing remains stable. Updated Qwen metadata and duplicate GRACE/Geometry of Truth entries do not constitute distinct new works.

T1.justification: The formal routing definitions in Sections 4.2–4.3 change from squared-L2 minimization to cosine maximization, which are not equivalent as written without normalization assumptions. The two geometric properties, ReFT map, robustness derivation, clustering algorithm and routing-accuracy definition otherwise remain substantively unchanged; no new proofs are added.

improvement.justification: v1's locality evidence primarily used random-pair separation and retained MMLU performance; v2 directly examines lexical confounding and router rejection. Together with the GRACE and Qwen-WISE comparisons, radius analysis and newly disclosed training settings, this substantially strengthens validation and reproducibility of the existing framework. Explicit limitations better bound its applicability. Removing the single-edit results and forgetting curve reduces some evidence, but the retained sequential evaluations preserve support for the main lifelong-editing claims.

A1.justification: Both PDFs describe RILKE under the same title and authorship. All pages, including the appendices, are readable, and the text, equations, tables and figures support comparison after matching relocated and renumbered material.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds ZsRE evaluation, baseline comparisons, hard-negative analysis, radius sensitivity, router activation checks and training-cost measurements.

before.justification: v1 reports original UnKE and EditEverything experiments, MMLU evaluations, intervention ablations, routing measurements and inference-latency results.

results.title: Representation Interventions Enable Lifelong Knowledge Memory Control in LLMs

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims: a first naturalistic document-level cross-lingual RSD benchmark and a substantial performance gap between synthetic and realistic evaluation.

C2.justification: Section 3 replaces the earlier emphasis on exceptionally poor EN-DE span agreement with a distinction between span overlap and label consistency. Section 6 adds document segmentation as a possible explanation for short-context encoders' stronger results. Appendix A.4 removes the explicit ranking-instability warning and the interpretation concerning missed omissions/additions.

D1.justification: v2 documents the annotation-run replacement and its reported agreement improvement in Section 3, footnote 6. Table 10 corrects LaBSE's stated parameter count from 500B to 500M. Prompts, annotation guidelines, hyperparameters, hardware and timing information, and code/data access links otherwise remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 224 multi-parallel Swiss government documents covering EN-DE, EN-FR, and EN-IT, together with the same iSTS-RSD languages and augmentation scenarios. Revised annotations do not expand or remove represented documents, domains, or tasks.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the corresponding main and appendix experiments: the same DiffAlign encoders, prompted and reasoning LLMs, fine-tuned LLMs, and ModernBERT variants participate. LaBSE's parameter-count correction does not establish a comparator replacement.

E3.justification: Section 3 reports replacing a poor EN-DE annotation run with a new annotator, substantially revising reference annotations used for evaluation. Table 2 also adds agreement over all token labels, including zeros, alongside existing span-based metrics. Model training budgets, dataset sizes, and testing procedures otherwise remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix A.4 revises the analysis of model sensitivity to annotator differences and removes v1's Figure 9 case study illustrating missed omissions/additions. The span-granularity examples in Figure 8 remain. The token-position analysis in Figure 5 is updated, while the projected-label audit and other supplementary analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version adds or revises seed reporting, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty estimation. Table 15 retains the same 100 encoder and 10 LLM timing measurements. The added human-agreement correlation is an evaluation metric.

E6.justification: SwissGov results and rankings change substantially. In Table 3, the EN-DE leader switches from Qwen3-Embedding 4B at 16.1 to LaBSE at 20.6, previously 12.5; Llama-3.1 405B changes from 2.4 to -0.8. Revised EN-DE references prevent interpreting these as same-setting model gains or losses. XLM-R+SimCSE's EN-FR and EN-IT scores also change from 9.3/24.6 to 10.0/23.4. Tables 2, 6, 7, and 14 and Figures 3, 5–7 contain revised results; iSTS-RSD scores remain unchanged.

M1.justification: Section 4 retains the same DiffAlign algorithm, few-shot prompting, LLM fine-tuning, encoder regression architecture and loss, and LLM-based label projection. The annotation revision does not introduce a new automatic detection method.

P1.justification: Rewriting is concentrated in annotation validation, the encoder/LLM discussion, and Appendix A.4, with small wording and header edits elsewhere. The overall section organization, methods exposition, and principal contribution narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 3 is redrawn with adjusted chart sizing and axes presentation. Table 2 regroups its metrics and adds an agreement row. v1's omission/addition Figure 9 is removed; its Figure 10 becomes v2's Figure 9, and Appendices B and C now share a page. These are localized presentation changes.

R1.justification: v2 adds Kreutzer et al. (2020) and Lavie et al. (2025) to contextualize annotation difficulty. The retained Sarti et al. (2025) citation shifts from supporting ranking-instability concerns to contextualizing agreement. The broader research positioning and novelty claims remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The task formulation, labeling definitions, IoU equation, and DiffAlign equation are unchanged. Applying the existing Spearman metric to all human labels introduces no new mathematical definition, derivation, theorem, or proof.

improvement.justification: Replacing the poor EN-DE annotation run addresses a serious consistency weakness in the paper's central benchmark. On the overlapping documents, English-side IoU rises from 11.17 to 23.98 and German-side IoU from 10.22 to 39.95 (Table 2). Reporting all-token human agreement also makes model results easier to contextualize. Removing Appendix A.4's ranking-instability warning weakens qualification, but the substantial annotation-quality repair and stronger validation outweigh that loss.

A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SwissGov-RSD research work. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices A–J are readable and support a reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

after.justification: v2 retains the original model experiments and reports revised annotation analyses and SwissGov-RSD evaluation results in the main text and appendices.

before.justification: v1 reports original human-annotation analyses and experiments evaluating encoders and LLMs on SwissGov-RSD and iSTS-RSD, including Table 3 and supplementary results.

results.title: SwissGov-RSD: A Human-annotated, Cross-lingual Benchmark for Token-level Recognition of Semantic Differences Between Related Documents

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion expand the claimed empirical scope from mathematical RLVR to mathematics, medicine and coding across 1.5B–32B models. v1's mathematical SOTA assertion is removed. The central geometry-aware initialization and stable, efficient adaptation contributions remain.

C2.justification: v3 substantially qualifies explanations that previously treated tail components as noise, KL spikes as establishing collapse's root cause, and GeoRA as strictly trust-region safe. It adds mask-complementarity and measured initialization-overhead interpretations. The OOD discussion also replaces v1's incorrect best-GPQA claim with strongest-or-near-strongest wording. The Limitations section is unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendices A–C add pseudocode, SVD profiling, alpha 32, all-linear adapter targets, AdamW/bfloat16, batch size 128, eight rollouts, KL coefficient 0.001, GPU configurations and task-specific verification rules. These substantially expand reproducibility information. However, Algorithm 1 uses an unscaled residual subtraction, conflicting with the alpha/r scaling retained in Equation (4).

E1.justification: v3 adds medical RLVR using AlphaMed19K with MedQA, MedMCQA and PubMedQA evaluation, and coding RLVR using Eurus-2-RL-Data with LiveCodeBench, HumanEval and MBPP evaluation. It also adds IFEval and TruthfulQA to OOD coverage. DeepMath-103K, GSM8K and HumanEval were already used in v1.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds the original pre-RLVR Base model as a comparator for both backbones. FullFT, SparseFT, LoRA, PiSSA and MiLoRA remain in the matched mathematical comparison. The new medical and coding comparisons use Base, FullFT and LoRA.

E3.justification: Added experiments introduce Qwen2.5-1.5B and Qwen3-32B configurations, medical test-split validation and option-matching rewards, and coding verification through executable test cases with a 2048-token response budget. Initialization profiling spans 8B–72B models. The retained mathematical setup still specifies GRPO, rank 16 and rho 0.2; newly disclosed settings do not establish changes to those existing experiments.

E4.justification: v3 adds mask-overlap analysis (Table 5), analysis of actual FullFT update spectra (Figure 6b), and initialization-cost profiling (Table 7). Appendix D supplies explicit rank and sparsity sweep curves for robustness that v1 only summarized. Existing initialization/mask ablations and learning-rate/KL stress tests are retained.

E5.justification: Appendix C.1 newly specifies a single random run; v1 gives no run count. No repeated-run uncertainty estimates or significance tests are added. This is newly disclosed run information, not evidence that the number of runs decreased.

E6.justification: Table 1 extensions and new Tables 2, 5, 7 and 8 add substantial results; for example, GeoRA's medical and coding averages are 73.69 and 79.65. Retained main per-task, efficiency, ablation and alignment table values are unchanged. Figure 3 also revises plotted step-500 accuracy: LoRA approximately 19.89 to 19.39 and GeoRA 22.29 to 22.69, while retaining their final values.

M1.justification: Section 3, Equations (1)–(8), retains the same mask union, top-r SVD initialization, frozen scaled residual and forward computation. The added pseudocode and randomized-SVD discussion document the method and implementation options without establishing a changed core procedure.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, experimental discussion, mechanism narrative and conclusion undergo substantial rewriting. Experiments are reorganized into setup, main results, stability/efficiency and ablation subsections, and Appendices A–D are introduced. The method exposition remains largely unchanged.

P2.justification: Table 1 adds Base rows and two OOD columns while removing the ID-average column; four new tables are introduced. Figure 3 changes from grouped bars to lines, Figure 6 expands to two panels, and Figure 7 and Algorithm 1 are added. Several retained displays are resized or relocated.

R1.justification: Section 2.2 adds continual-learning and multi-task PEFT references, and the expanded experiments introduce benchmark and domain citations. The main positioning around RLVR geometry and spectral PEFT remains. Author, year and publication changes for existing references do not represent new cited works.

T1.justification: Appendix B adds a Frobenius-optimality proposition for truncated Geo-SVD, adapter-gradient formulas in Equation (12), and computational complexity analysis. Its function-preservation proposition largely restates the initialization identity already explained in v1. These are limited mathematical additions.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially strengthens the paper's assessability and supporting evidence: Base comparisons clarify forgetting, actual FullFT update spectra better support the low-rank motivation, and Appendix C fills major reproducibility gaps. Medical/coding evaluations and initialization profiling directly test broader applicability and practical efficiency, while interpretations become better qualified. Single-run evidence still limits confidence, and Algorithm 1 introduces a scaling inconsistency, but these limitations do not outweigh the substantial gains.

A1.justification: Both PDFs describe GeoRA and contain readable, matchable methods, experiments, equations, tables and figures. All pages were inspected. v1 ends with references and has no appendices; v3 includes readable Appendices A–D.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and adds medical and coding evaluations, mask-overlap measurements, initialization profiling and extended model evaluations, including results in Appendices B–D.

before.justification: v1 reports original RLVR training outcomes, benchmark evaluations, efficiency measurements, ablations and geometric analyses in Tables 1–4 and Figures 3–6.

results.title: GeoRA: Geometry-Aware Low-Rank Adaptation for RLVR

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction replace claims of maintaining competitive performance with an efficiency-accuracy Pareto framing, qualifying the performance claim around a tradeoff. The novelty, analyzability, plug-and-play, and compression contributions remain unchanged; logical-reasoning coverage was already claimed in v1.

C2.justification: New discussion interprets the shared-backbone results as evidence against a pretraining-only explanation and argues that inference savings offset training overhead. Appendix G strengthens the termination explanation into an asserted intrinsic continuous-space difficulty, without a new causal test. Existing limitations and case interpretations are retained.

D1.justification: v3 adds homepage and model-collection access links and documents hardware, epoch allocation, and measured costs for the training-time comparison. Original implementation hyperparameters remain unchanged. The new GPQA/ProsQA evaluation receives only a general statement that implementation details are consistent with the existing setup.

E1.justification: v3 retains GSM8k-Aug, GSM-Hard, SVAMP, MultiArith, and MATH, and adds actual evaluations on GPQA and ProsQA in Appendix F. These extend the evaluated coverage from mathematical problems to scientific question answering and logical reasoning.

E2.justification: The original comparator sets remain intact. New Tables 8-9 reuse Coconut, CODI, and CoLaR-2, already evaluated in v1. The documented differences concern backbone settings and task coverage; no comparator-algorithm revision is specified.

E3.justification: Appendix E adds a controlled comparison placing RoT and three baselines on Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct, addressing the differing backbones in retained Table 2. Appendix D introduces training-time measurements with matched three-epoch budgets, batch size 16, and one H20 GPU. Existing experimental protocols are retained.

E4.justification: Appendices D-E add analyses of training overhead and whether backbone differences explain RoT's advantage, substantially extending the efficiency and attribution evidence. Existing stage, projection-head, rendering, decoding, and case analyses remain unchanged. Appendix G adds discussion, not another termination experiment.

E5.justification: The five-seed/95% confidence-interval statement and existing uncertainty entries remain unchanged. New appendix tables report point values, as earlier appendix ablation tables already did; no changed run counts or statistical estimation procedures are specified.

E6.justification: Tables 7-9 add training times of 56.1 hours for RoT versus 36.9 for SFT-CoT, VLM-based comparator results including CoLaR-2's 45.3 average versus RoT's retained 55.4, and RoT Pass@1 scores of 60.5 on GPQA and 100.0 on ProsQA. Original Tables 1-6 and plotted findings are unchanged. The new backbone results are additional evaluations, not corrections or same-setting performance changes.

M1.justification: The rendering procedure, visual projection head, two-stage training, losses, and dynamic/fixed-budget decoding procedures remain unchanged. Applying existing baselines to another backbone does not establish a change to RoT.

P1.justification: Changes include limited abstract/introduction wording, author-order and affiliation edits, and four new appendix sections with an expanded contents list. The case study becomes Appendix H, with updated cross-references. The existing narrative is largely retained.

P2.justification: v3 adds three compact appendix tables and a title-page resource strip. Figure 2 moves earlier, some tables become more compact, and appendix material shifts. Original figure content and existing table structures remain intact.

R1.justification: v3 adds the GPQA reference by Rein et al. and expands discussion connecting termination difficulties to the already cited LVR work. The related-work section and central novelty positioning otherwise remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The loss equations, termination definition, and special-token normalization remain unchanged. Appendix G's continuous-space explanation introduces no formal assumption, theorem, derivation, or proof.

improvement.justification: Table 8 addresses an important confound in v1's central baseline comparison by using the same backbone. Table 7 makes training overhead measurable, while Table 9 supplies evidence for previously claimed non-mathematical applicability. Together these substantially strengthen empirical support and transparency. Sparse task-specific documentation and absent displayed uncertainty in the new comparisons limit their strength, but do not outweigh these gains.

A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Render-of-Thought. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support comparison, including the image-based case studies. The original case-study appendix moves from D to H.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds training-time measurements, evaluations using a shared backbone, and GPQA/ProsQA results in Tables 7-9.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, training and decoding ablations, inference timings, and latent-representation case studies in the main text and appendices.

results.title: Render-of-Thought: Rendering Textual Chain-of-Thought as Images for Visual Latent Reasoning

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion replace the attribution of hard-negative gains to superior LLM understanding of negation with an explanation emphasizing audio-space separation and word-order sensitivity shared with CLAP. This substantially revises a central explanatory claim while retaining the headline retrieval-performance claims.

C2.justification: V3 rejects the earlier contrast between compositional OEA processing and bag-of-content CLAP processing: its controls find exclusion-sensitive word-order effects in every tested encoder. It also explains that exclusion clauses attract excluded content rather than cleanly suppressing it, clarifies sample-based validation limits and recasts comparison with real search-query distributions as future work.

D1.justification: V3 adds encoder and deployment details, including audio-encoder dimensions, bidirectional attention and inactive speech-generation components, plus implementation details for the new controls. It revises dataset-release and access statements and removes annotator recruitment/payment details. Core training hyperparameters and generation prompts are retained.

E1.justification: Training and evaluation datasets remain unchanged. Appendix O extends testing to word-order-corrupted queries and matched queries with exclusion clauses removed, adding controlled input scenarios within the existing AudioCaps, Clotho and MECAT coverage.

E2.justification: The original benchmark comparator sets remain unchanged. Appendix O.3 newly evaluates a pre-transformer mean-pooling control, reporting R@1 approximately zero, while the new mechanism comparisons reuse M2D-CLAP, MGA-CLAP and LAION-CLAP.

E3.justification: Appendix O introduces fixed-checkpoint diagnostic protocols on 630 AudioCaps, 542 Clotho and 409 MECAT pairs: audio-only separation, matched exclusion-clause removal and identical word shuffles across encoders. Benchmark-curation descriptions also change from sampled rejection/regeneration to post-hoc query validation and human-guided threshold calibration. These are reported protocol revisions, without evidence that the original benchmark experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: V2's proposed explanation for hard-negative gains was largely interpretive. V3 adds a substantial mechanism-analysis suite separating audio geometry, exclusion-clause effects and word-order sensitivity, including cross-model shuffle controls that challenge the earlier explanation.

E5.justification: V3 adds paired Wilcoxon signed-rank testing for audio separation and shuffle effects, including dataset-specific significance and comparisons of exclusion-specific structure contributions. This substantially extends inferential reporting beyond the retained human/LLM validation statistics. No repeated-training-run or multi-seed evaluation is introduced.

E6.justification: The original retrieval tables retain their values. New Tables 17–20 report diagnostic outcomes, including mean audio distances of 0.317 versus 0.223 for OEA and M2D-CLAP, deterioration when exclusion clauses are present, and OEA exclusionary Δ-Rank falling from 22.5 to -7.2 after shuffling. These are newly reported diagnostic results, not improvements over v2 under established identical settings.

M1.justification: The shared backbone, LoRA adapters, projection heads, pooling and contrastive objective remain unchanged. Appendix O explicitly evaluates a released checkpoint without retraining; the revised human-curation descriptions concern benchmark construction and validation.

P1.justification: The explanatory narrative and appendix organization are substantially revised. Section 5.4 is absorbed into appendix discussions, Appendices H–M are reordered, the query-distribution discussion becomes a bias analysis, and the conclusion, limitations, efficiency and scaling discussions are rewritten.

P2.justification: Figure 2 corrects the second training input from 'Text Batch' to 'Audio Batch'; Figures 1 and 3 are unchanged. Four diagnostic tables are added, duplicate efficiency displays are consolidated into a compact appendix table, and several tables are reformatted or relocated. The overall visual design remains stable.

R1.justification: V3 adds Wang et al. (2024), the E5 embedding work, and invokes E5/BGE literature to contextualize retrieval scaling. The main related-work sections and other cited works remain, while the claimed distinction from CLAP text processing is narrowed.

T1.justification: Appendix O introduces mathematical diagnostic contrasts, including ΔΔ-Rank for clause effects and S(m), the exclusionary shuffle gap minus the positive-query shuffle gap. The original loss and retrieval-metric definitions remain unchanged; no theorem or proof is added.

improvement.justification: V3 addresses an important weakness: v2 inferred specialized negation understanding from retrieval advantages without directly testing that explanation. Appendix O supplies controlled evidence that challenges this account, and the abstract and conclusion adopt a more qualified mechanism claim. Validation descriptions also become more explicit. New reporting defects remain—Table 19's positive-query gap disagrees with its displayed values, and Appendix L mislabels a human–LLM correlation as inter-annotator agreement—but these local inconsistencies do not outweigh the substantial improvement in testing and qualifying the central explanation.

A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Omni-Embed-Audio research. All 18 pages of v2 and 19 pages of v3, including their appendices, are readable and support matching text, equations, figures and tables.

after.justification: V3 retains these empirical results and adds audio-separation, negation-removal and query-shuffling experiments in Appendix O.

before.justification: V2 reports original retrieval experiments, human and LLM query validation, dataset-overlap analysis and inference-efficiency measurements.

results.title: Omni-Embed-Audio: Leveraging Multimodal LLMs for Robust Audio-Text Retrieval

C1.justification: The central contribution changes from specialized pretrained models with superior retrieval/recommendation performance to a benchmark of existing semantic encoders. v2 adds headline claims about disagreement with MTEB, task-dependent scaling, and Amazon-C4's usefulness as a proxy for real complex queries.

C2.justification: v1's explanations of BLAIR training benefits and curriculum-related overfitting are replaced by interpretations involving encoder discriminability, downstream complexity, metadata noise, and complex intent. v2 also introduces substantive limitations concerning English-only coverage, restricted model/category coverage, and incomplete review collection, plus failure analysis.
